This is part two of Brand as Software.

When I joined Ramp ten months ago, my two senior brand designers were making decks and whitepapers. It made sense. They were the ones with judgment and taste and craft, and the company needed those assets. But I wanted them to build the brand system, preparing us for what turned out to be an incredible year of growth and new products at Ramp. So I took them off the decks and whitepapers right away. Contractors took over the production, and my designers got their time back.

What I want from AI, and what I want it to give creative teams, is time: time for deep work, time to let ideas simmer and marinate, and time to go deep on the things AI cannot do well. Where we give our attention, and how we spend our time, will determine the quality of our ideas and execution.

Time is scarce. We have ancient brains, and we’re using an alien technology that pushes our attention further every week. Most of us get three or four hours of solid concentration a day before the brain starts to fizzle. Parkinson’s Law says work expands to fill the time you give it, and sometimes what you think takes a month takes a week. But I bet a lot of creative teams are one more week, or one more month, away from taking their best idea to the next level. What’s stopping them is the constant urgent requests from every team.

When your creative team is making the same assets over and over, it’s wasted talent. When you pair creatives with builders who codify the team’s quality and execution, especially for repetitive work like documents and decks, you can scale creativity and protect the rare talent that makes a company stand out.

Here’s how we set up brand as infrastructure at Ramp, what we’re learning, and what the time we got back made possible.

Cover the production, protect the time

Like I joked in the last essay, the more I use AI, the more I see the past of my career as laughable monkey behavior: hunched over a keyboard, pressing CMD+C and CMD+V from one rectangle to the next. It’s silly to call this “work.” Give it to the machines and get back your time.

Bringing in contractors was the first step, and it was a staffing decision before it was an AI project. If I had asked my designers to evolve the brand system on top of an unchanged production queue, I would have given them a second job, with no time to go deep on anything. The production still had to get done.

One of the designers we brought in, Kyla, showed me the possibility of how designers can use AI. By her second week, she had used the AI tools at Ramp to build a tool that automated about 90% of our whitepaper work. Then she came to me and asked: that team has the tool now, what do you want me to work on instead? That’s the future. The second step was making sure that production work didn’t disappear once it shipped. Normally a deck or one-pager has the shelf life of a banana. We now have the technology where the good decisions and good output get codified into the agent as skills, guidelines. We create multiple 10/10 examples in Figma, so that the agents can learn what approved, good work means to the brand team. It has to pattern-match excellence.

It helps to be precise about which work this covers. There are decks that agents can create so anyone at the company can self-serve. Others need to be hand-crafted, like the one for your company conference. The hand-crafted work still belongs to designers, and it should get their full attention. The best part is what happens when that deck is done: its quality gets added back into the brand system, where the agents can see it. Now you have a new template, new animations and new storytelling that are part of your brand infrastructure, and the standard of good work elevates everyone.

That’s brand as infrastructure. Designers make creative decisions. Builders turn the repeatable ones into tools the rest of the company can use. The designers’ time goes to the decisions nobody has made yet. They have time to invent the future, imagine, and dream. Rather than having a short turnaround time to execute good work, they have more time to push the idea further.

I believe protecting this resource, nurturing it, will help companies stand out and win the marketplace.

Judgment is human. Repetition is software.

The Michelin-star vending machine

At Ramp, we have an internal Slack agent called Ramp Creative that makes on-brand decks, whitepapers, one-pagers, print material of all kinds, and product graphics. It can also edit images, like changing a $ to € or swapping a customer’s logo. We’re working on getting it to make product demos, reels and videos too.

The person asking for a deck wants something they can use, edit and refine. Humans still desire control. They shouldn’t have to learn the finer points of typography, hunt through three libraries, or become an expert at prompting before they can do their job.

I quickly learned that it’s not about making a bunch of tools for everyone. Tools are personal and should be an extension of the person with expertise.

What everyone wants is a Michelin-star vending machine: press a button and get something excellent. That means the brand team does the hard, strategic work before the requester ever places an order.

Most creative teams have run like a sandwich counter. An order comes in, the team puts the sandwich together, and it goes out. The best creative teams of the next decade will run test kitchens, with the time to let ideas marinate, to experiment, to find out what works and what fails. Their best experiments go into the vending machine.

A fair question is whether this system leads to settling for good enough. Quite the opposite. I avoid the word “template” because people hear lower quality: it’s just a template, so whatever. A Michelin-star vending machine only works if what goes into it is the team’s best work.

Here’s how a request moves through it. Someone asks Ramp Creative for an asset in Slack. The agent picks an approved skill, which is a set of instructions and rules for that format, including what can and cannot change. It fills the layout with the requester’s words and approved images, a renderer turns that into the finished file, and automated tests check for broken dimensions, missing fonts and overflowing copy before the asset comes back in Slack. Behind all of that, the brand team designs and approves the 10/10 examples in Figma, the skills live in Dojo, our internal library for sharing them, and the agent runs on Inspect.

When someone asks for something the agent doesn’t have a skill or template for, it vibecodes an attempt. We set up an automation that identifies an asset missing its core ingredients, adds it to a database, and pings a designer. The designer has 24 to 48 hours to turn the vibecoded slop into 10/10 examples of that asset, so the agent can pattern-match better. Then a skill formats the Figma file so it’s ready to encode into Ramp Creative.

I realized the bottleneck as I was writing this. A designer still has to make each new 10/10 example by hand, even if a senior designer approves it in under a minute. Next, the agent makes 30 versions in Figma, and the designer only comments: this works, this doesn’t. Approve the work, get it in the system.

For the formats we support, 80% isn’t good enough. An agent that gets people most of the way repeats the same bullshit we’re trying to escape: people generate something, knowing a designer is there to save the day. If this agent can’t give people 100% of what they need, I’d rather hire 10 production designers cranking out finished assets every day.

Reliability is the price of entry. I’ve learned that if the agent doesn’t deliver within a couple of attempts, people work around it, prompt their own AI, and the brand-as-software philosophy fails.

The UK launch

Sabrina from marketing pushed Ramp Creative to produce and localize more than 80% of the assets for our UK launch. The brand team had already made the design and creative decisions. Sabrina could self-serve the work she needed, from product graphics to decks to documents.

Before, the brand team would have had to compromise. Do we work on the UK launch because it’s the most important thing right now, or do we work on the conference or the brand or the 100 other urgent requests? That’s the tradeoff this system helps us avoid. This is the challenge of nearly every brand team from the past two decades.

OnRamp Conference

OnRamp is @tryramp yearly conference for finance leaders and its biggest brand moment. In 2026, it welcomed more than 1,200 people to San Francisco and 2,500 more online, and it’s where Ramp showed its product roadmap, including the first public look at Glass.

If you’ve ever had to do events, there is never enough people or time. Last minute requests, no matter how much you prepare, are normal. So, we used the agent to make a lot of edits, fixes, and assets completely self-serve.

People ask me how, in my ten months here, we pulled off a full brand refresh in four weeks and branded Ramp Labs, Stack, Glass, Inspect and Router while Ramp was also shipping Bill Pay, Accounts Receivable, international expansion and other projects. Each of those needed landing pages, assets, demos, copy, videos, and product graphics.

One answer is talent, which Ramp is overflowing with. Second, I am insanely grateful for our agency partner, Common Reality, and my team for focusing on execution. Overhauling the brand system in four weeks enabled everyone to do better work. We had fewer reviews with other teams because of it. It’s not that my team didn’t want to work on core launches like Bill Pay or UK Launch; it was really about opportunity cost, and new flagship products like Glass and Inspect allowed us to keep pushing the edges of our system.

One last example. Sophie, from the SEO team that works on Router, uses Ramp Creative thoroughly. She self-serves everything she needs from new launch assets to landing pages to product graphics and social posts. Internally, we look at this agent as a product, with customers that we need to take care of. As new assets are needed, the system gets smarter because it pattern-matches to other work. The goal is to keep feeding back good layouts, compositions, and work to the system.

Deep work needs an environment, resources, and protection. Brand as infrastructure changes the DNA of a company. And for too long, creative teams just weren’t allowed to do this or had to burn out and white-knuckle it all. That isn’t sustainable, especially for the era we’re entering where anything can be built by anyone.

Artists, builders, and brand designers are the rare talent that will make your company stand out.

What would you do with more time?

One of my favorite projects at Ramp is Inspect, a cloud coding agent that the engineering team built internally. It handles over 80% of our PRs, and it’s one of the coolest things I’ve seen and used. We opened up beta access on October 27.

When I started on the launch, I found out that Sabrina had already spoken to prospects and design partners. I interviewed Nico, the engineering lead, and his team. I also interviewed Marcelo, a product designer who loves using Inspect.

In the old world, this is where meetings about meetings start: endless documents, long Slack messages, stakeholder reviews, 50 comments to address in Notion or Docs, and too many chefs added into the kitchen. Because there was conviction and clarity on what Inspect is and who it’s for, we skipped most of that theater.

I’ve been honing a bundle of skills that take me from research to a brief, to brand strategy, to a campaign platform, and I used them on everything Sabrina, Nico, Marcelo and the team had told me. I put the brief together in minutes. I got Sabrina and Nico aligned in a few days. I briefed the designers by the end of the week. Three weeks to come up with multiple, strong directions is intense — plus landing page, copywriting, and assets — but that’s how we operate, and we were able to keep the quality high.

Why? Because it’s not that I’m relying on AI to give me an answer. I’m using this tool to help access parts of my past, my career, and my brain. I can tell quickly whether something feels right or wrong. People call that taste, but you don’t award yourself taste, any more than you award yourself a Michelin star. It’s earned after years and years of hard work, and almost arrives late. What you start with is a point of view.

The brief drew on Sabrina’s customer conversations and the people who build and use Inspect. I sent Nico a dozen questions in a Google Doc, and his engineers answered them. I also scraped every past conversation and Notion document about Inspect. The agent came back with three brand strategy options.

The AI companies scraped the internet. They didn’t scrape my Dropbox: decades of client work, decks I rewrote and rebuilt, thousands of essay drafts with comments from editors that refined the work, and 60,000 images I’ve saved over my career, now indexed and tagged. From those, I pulled six art direction worlds to explore with the team. Speed comes less from the technology than from the person with a point of view able to bend the tool to their needs.

It’s like looking at a design portfolio: it only takes me a few seconds.

What I care about is what we did with the time. Sabrina, Nico and I got to banter and question the messaging, language, framing, words and outcomes. I got to really understand why Marcelo loves using Inspect as a product designer and learned how other people in the company use it directly in Slack.

The brand team had more time to explore directions, to question how Inspect connects to the Ramp brand system overall, and to push the work. People are probably realizing that the bottleneck to excellence was always the issue: too many chefs in the kitchen, but more importantly, the wrong chefs. On the Inspect launch, a few experts trusted each other to do their jobs well. Collaboration, trust, and respect for craft will never go out of style.

So many good ideas die because teams thrash at the end instead of the beginning. If everyone thrashes in the first 20%, the bad ideas come out early, and there’s time left to execute the good one.

What leaders have to change

The deeper problem is how decisions get made.

Giving everyone more tools can intensify an old problem: the ability to generate something becomes another way to overrule the person responsible for making it good. That’s why I think brand teams should be set up like security or infrastructure teams.

The comparison has limits. Bad design doesn’t sink a business overnight the way a breach can. The damage over time is slower: one year you ship the new rebrand, and by next year, you look like three different companies. With AI, people will generate random assets, thinking it looks good, or worse, “fine,” and ship it. There’s no way for a brand team to monitor everything that goes out the door.

Design and creative output in tech is treated like movies or fashion. Everyone can have an opinion about it. Ask any professional writer or photographer and they know what I’m talking about. Because people can read, they think they can write. Good writing makes it look easy, and now that AI makes production look easy too, it’s tempting to believe output can stand in for skill, taste, and experience.

What I want to borrow from a security team is the way companies fund and trust it. Security gets dedicated people, clear ownership, a budget, the authority to say no, and accountability when something goes wrong. If a brand team is made up of artists and builders, and treated that way, what it’s accountable for is simple: make the brand easy to love and impossible to misuse.

In a more truthful tone: no one tells the security team to go fuck themselves.

At Ramp, that now means Ramp Creative has a dedicated backend engineer and a designer, and I’m in the codebase myself. To be honest, a lot of our best work from this year isn’t in the system yet. That’s what the people are for.

But historically brand and creative teams are at the end of the line. The last to know and the first to get blamed. When there is no clarity or strategic thinking from the people who start a project or need something from the brand team, the creatives have to fix it. They have to act as detectives, journalists, and therapists. And they have no time to go deep. In many ways, brand and creative teams have been treated and spoken to like LLMs for decades. All of that is about to fundamentally change.

AI can make the sandwich counter faster, or it can give the team a test kitchen, and leaders decide which. Fund designers and the builders beside them with committed time. Cover production while the system is built, and settle upfront who makes the final creative call. Then protect the time you get back so the team can make better work and feed its best decisions back into the system. Everyone’s work starts from a higher standard.

The north star is simple: Incredible craft at incredible scale.

None of this replaces collaboration. I love working with PMs, PMMs and engineers who respect what I do, cheer on good ideas, and share signals that help me adapt the idea. If they have time to talk to customers and gather signals, that’s exactly what my team needs to begin. I can scrape the docs and Gong calls, use a set of skills to form a brief, and then we can spend our time together debating the brief and thrashing early.

I bet you’re moving faster, but not going deeper, and still looking to Twitter and other companies to borrow their success. A company can keep growing while it becomes boring and unimaginative. Success hides failures. The ZIRP era is gone, you can’t throw money at the problem anymore, and I think employees and consumers will be quicker to leave brands they no longer believe in. You need a story, a point of view, and the execution to make it real. This is where competition is going to get spicy, and I want more of it.

Build the infrastructure now

I don’t have a crystal ball, but I’d rather we build for next year’s landscape than today’s. This is also a great moment in time to connect brand to real business outcomes. For my entire career, “measuring brand” was a moving target. Sure, share of “branded search” or brand awareness is measurable, but it’s one of many metrics, and doesn’t always paint the full picture. Meta and Google are the tails that wag your strategy and spend.

Now, brand can prove that this agent creates a deck that costs, maybe, a dollar, versus $100 an hour for a person. This isn’t about replacing humans; this is about putting your best creative talent on hard problems instead.

It’s all about opportunity cost: if you weren’t doing this, what would you be doing instead? Brand design is arguably the rarest talent in tech; there are plenty of engineers and marketers. Why, then, are they spending hours fixing other people’s mistakes? This team is about inventing futures that no one is thinking about.

I recently connected with our SVP of Sales, Max Freeman, and audited how his best sellers work. From how they make decks, what they prompt, how they sell — this is a design challenge. Empathy, user experience, and imagining what better looks like. Now we can take all of that work, get the best brand talent on it, and level up everyone else in the org. The agent levels up. The system introduces high quality at scale for everyone. Great design is not an asset, it’s what it enables people to do with their time.

Start with decks, whitepapers, and the small tasks that add up, like resizing logos or swapping customer logos. These are important for a business, but they should not be eating up your creative team’s time. It’s like having Olympic athletes refilling water bottles.

Pair the brand/creative team with engineers. In essence, you are building a software product. It cannot suffice as a tool. It has to become a system of tools, agents, skills, libraries, guidelines, recipes, evaluations, and tests.

Imagine you’re a startup and you have a fresh new brand. This infrastructure can help every new hire represent the brand well in their work. Imagine you rebranded a year or two later. Well, you feed that work back into the system, and the entire score of music updates. Rather than taking months applying the new brand to every channel and surface, you treat the brand like a software update.

This is all very very fun for me. It’s like watching a history book evolve in real time. I was always confused by how companies with so much potential and money operated. I understood all the drama that tech spews on Twitter about every function or team. AI is the wrecking ball for this house of cards, these illusions we’ve been defending for years.

Companies need to fundamentally reimagine how they operate. Careers are going to be wildly different. Job titles will get ever more confusing. The only thing that matters right now is adaptability and execution, kindness and collaboration.

Many companies make noise, but who will make music?

I believe that begins and ends with your brand and creative teams.

More power to them.

A heartfelt thank you to Caroline Donofrio for editing this essay, and to Mint Zhai, Eleanor Ngai, and Stephen Ong for the beautiful demos that brought it to life.

Massive thank you to Emerline Ji, Drew Minns, Burak Aslan, and Mary Jiang for making Ramp Creative possible; I could not have done this without you.

Enormous gratitude to Mint Zhai, Kyla Arsadjaja, Claire Chen, and Coco Yuan for your 10/10 design work, and to Mark Weaver and Aodan Reddy for keeping the bar high.

Thank you to Diego Zaks for believing in this endeavor, allowing me to fail and fail until we got it right.

Special thanks to dear friends who read early drafts and provided useful feedback: Behzod Sirjani, Mike Smith, Sean Blanda, Lucas Crespo, Flora Guo, Elizabeth Lin, Katie Siu, Mark Johnson, and Michael Casebolt.

And please check out my latest podcast episode with Ridd from Dive Club where I share the demos, tools and thinking behind this essay in more depth.

entry.title: Investing in Isomorphic
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @eriktorenberg（Erik Torenberg） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

Drug discovery and development will be one of the largest opportunities for AI. Pharma is already an enormous industry, but there’s still too much disease and too few treatments. The goal is to make better medicines faster and at lower cost, and to treat disease we can’t today.

That is why we’re excited to invest in Isomorphic Labs. Founded by Sir Demis Hassabis, Isomorphic is building an AI-native pharmaceutical company with a mission to solve all disease.

It always starts with the team. Beyond founding and chairing DeepMind and serving as Chief Scientist at Alphabet, Demis (@demishassabis) helped deliver a breakthrough in protein structure prediction that earned him the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. President Max Jaderberg (@maxjaderberg) is a preeminent machine learning researcher and operator. Together, they’ve assembled an exceptional team of AI researchers, engineers, biologists, chemists, and clinicians. Their collective research achievements are remarkable. Their culture is organized around demanding scientific goals and measurable progress.

Isomorphic has brought the pace and ambition of a frontier AI lab to one of the hardest challenges in science, the work of developing new medicines.

Isomorphic’s scientific heritage is AlphaFold, but its work extends well beyond protein structure prediction. The Isomorphic Labs Drug Design Engine (IsoDDE) brings together a suite of models to predict molecular structures and binding, assess drug properties and toxicity, map biological interactions, and design candidate molecules, with reasoning models coordinating the work and helping prioritize which molecules to make and test.

In drug discovery, being faster, cheaper and more effective keeps paying off. In many knowledge work use cases, a model below the frontier might be “good enough” to do the job, so we see diminishing returns to intelligence. But with medicines, we don’t want to settle for “good enough.” Drugs can always get better, and Isomorphic continues to define the frontier.

Isomorphic has emerged as a leading platform, underscored by its partnerships with Eli Lilly, Novartis and Johnson & Johnson as well as its own drug programs. Without giving it all away, here’s one anecdote about Isomorphic’s progress: its AI design agent was able to search and optimize molecular designs over 2-4 days, progressing computationally through iterations that would traditionally require 1-3 months each in the lab. There’s more to come!

We’re particularly excited about how Isomorphic is connecting these efforts as a vertically integrated platform. The ambition extends across the development lifecycle - choosing promising biological targets, optimizing molecules, and ultimately bringing medicines through clinical trials. Better predictions translate to better experiments, which inform the next round of models and designs. This loop compounds as the company takes on more programs.

If Isomorphic can improve the probability of success while reducing development time and cost, more diseases and patient populations become viable to serve. Isomorphic has the potential to be among the most important pharmaceutical companies in the world. The ultimate measure of that progress will be medicines that safely and effectively help patients.

Partnering with Demis, Max and Isomorphic on the mission means a lot to all of us at a16z.

For me, this is personal. My family has lost loved ones to heart disease and leukemia too soon, and every family has stories like this. When I look at my two children, I hope their generation will have a very different experience of health and aging. I’d love for them to live healthy lives well past 100. Isomorphic makes us optimistic about a healthier future.

More healthy years with the people you love. It’s hard to think of a more important application of AI.

Thanks to @justin_kahl and @CarolineGoggs for coauthoring this with me.

entry.title: 零路考拿美国驾照！中国驾照换领新泽西州（NJ）驾照保姆级指南
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @rwayne（Roland.W） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

最近准备去美东一趟，顺便把新泽西州（New Jersey）的驾照搞定。至于美国驾照的用处，懂的都懂（无论是自驾、当身份证件还是日常使用都非常方便）。

目前来看，支持用中国驾照直接换领或免路考的州主要有华盛顿州、新墨西哥州和新泽西州。其中，新泽西州算是门槛相对最低的，持有中国驾照可以直接免去路考，只需通过笔试即可拿证。我结合了多位网友的实战经验，整理出这份完整攻略，希望对有需要的朋友有所帮助！

一、 考前预约与准备

  1. 官网提前预约：一定要提前在新泽西州 MVC（机动车辆委员会）官网预约 “Initial Permit” 类别，能省去现场大量排队时间。
    考点推荐：根据网友反馈，Edison 或 Bayonne 考点的现场工作人员相对比较友好，推荐优先选择。

  1. 提前打印并填写表格：强烈建议提前在官网下载 BA-208 表格，在家里提前填好并打印出来。
    省时秘籍：建议直接提前填好并准备 2 份 BA-208 表格（办理 Permit 和正式驾照各需一份），现场预计能节省将近一半的时间！

二、 核心材料清单（凑齐“6分”身份证明）

新泽西州 MVC 审核材料的核心逻辑是凑齐 6 分身份证明（6 Points of ID）。出发前请务必反复检查以下材料：

  1. 护照原件（含有效签证及 I-94 记录）。
  2. 地址证明（Proof of Address）：可使用近一个月内的银行账单（Bank Statement）或信用卡账单（Credit Card Statement），需打印成纸质版。
    💡 实操小技巧：如果你目前不住在新泽西州，可以提前把银行账单地址暂时改成新泽西州朋友家的地址；等新的月度账单出炉后打印出来带去办理，办完驾照后再改回原地址即可。
  3. SSN（社会安全号）：有 SSN：必须携带 SSN 实体卡原件。
    无 SSN：完全没关系，现场找工作人员签一份无 SSN 的宣誓书（Affidavit）即可。
  4. 中国驾照原件及认证翻译件：原件要求：务必检查中国驾照外面的塑封皮完好无损，千万不能有破裂或拆封痕迹；同时建议**中国驾照拿满 1 年（即过了实习期）**再来换领，否则现场有概率会被卡。
    翻译件要求：千万不要自己 DIY 翻译！ 已经有不少朋友因为自己翻译格式不合规被拒。我已经整理好了合规的翻译件模板，有需要的朋友可以关注我私信获取。

  1. 其他补充材料：如果上述部分材料不全，可以对照文末附上的《MVC 官方 6 分身份证明材料清单》准备相应的替代文件。

三、 MVC 现场办理全流程（约 2 小时拿证）

只要材料齐全、提前填好表，从进门到拿到临时驾照全程大约只需 2 小时：

  • Step 1：签到与填表（办 Permit）
    进门到前台（Reception），工作人员会让你填写申请 Permit 的 BA-208 表格。如果你已经提前在家填好签字了，这步就能直接省去，直接给工作人员看即可。
  • Step 2：资料预审（ID Check）
    在前台取号后，排队进行 ID Check 并提交材料。工作人员核对无误后，拿着号码坐等叫号。
  • Step 3：办理 Permit 与缴费
    叫到号后去对应窗口提交材料。工作人员会确认你的换证资格并现场拍照（这次拍照仅用于系统建档，不是最终驾照上的照片）。现场缴纳 10 美元 申请费（现金、刷卡均可）。⚠️ 注意：缴费后工作人员会问你 “今天是否参加笔试（Knowledge Test）？”，请直接回答 “Yes”。
  • Step 4：参加笔试与视力测试
    拿着材料走到笔试区（如 18 号窗口）递交材料，上机参加笔试。笔试通过后，直接在同窗口完成简单的视力测试（可戴眼镜），随后等待工作人员叫名字领取盖有“考试通过”标记的文件。
  • Step 5：二次取号与预审（办正式驾照）
    考完别急着走！回到前台再次领取申请表（此时用上你提前备好的第二份 BA-208 表格），告知工作人员已通过笔试、现在要直接办理 Driver License（正式驾照）。取号后再次排队通过一次 ID Check，核对无误后等待叫号。
  • Step 6：缴费、拍证件照、拿临时驾照
    叫到号后去窗口提交材料、拍摄正式的驾照照片，并缴纳 28.63 美元 制卡费。缴费完成后，当场就会发给你一张纸质临时驾照（Temporary License），拿着它就可以直接合法上路开车了！

四、 考试细节与拿证小贴士

1. 关于上机笔试（Knowledge Test）

  • 题量与及格线：共 50 道选择题，每答完一道就会当场显示对错；只要累计答对 40 道题，系统就会自动结束考试并提示通过。
  • 语言与答题技巧：建议考前花 2~3 天刷一下题库。考试为触屏操作，支持选择中文考试；但部分题目的中文机翻可能有歧义，考试过程中可以随时切换中英文对照，确保看懂题意再作答。遇到不确定的题目可以先跳过，挑自己有把握的先做。

2. 关于视力测试（Vision Test）

  • 这里的测视力机器和国内不太一样：额头必须紧紧贴压在机器顶部的感应区，里面的屏幕才会亮起显示内容。支持戴眼镜测试，哪怕单眼看清楚也完全没问题。

3. 关于实体卡邮寄

  • 正式的塑料实体驾照会在 12~14 天左右 邮寄到家。
  • 💡 转寄技巧：在窗口登记信息时，你的居住地址（Residential Address）和邮寄地址（Mailing Address）是可以分开填写的。如果你不在新泽西长住，完全可以填写一个方便收信的转寄地址。

entry.title: How I got 3M views with AI slideshows and Fable 5.2
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @EianLu（Eian） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

By the end of this guide you will have one finished 6-slide AI UGC slideshow, five variations of it and a full week of posts scheduled. It is a method you can repeat on any app or product, on any platform that supports slideshows. What you get is a repeatable way to make good slideshows fast.

The slideshow comes out of one simple loop and the loop is what this article is about:

  1. Find a slideshow format that is already working for someone else.
  2. Have Claude Fable 5.2 take it apart and explain why it works.
  3. Rebuild it around my app, slide by slide.
  4. Turn the one that works into five or six variations.
  5. Schedule the batch in Postiz and read the numbers a week later.

Here is what you need to follow along:
A Claude account with Claude Fable 5.2 selected, which is the current top model An image generator (use the best one you have access to)
Canva or CapCut for the text overlay. 5 to 10 screenshots of the app or product you are promoting.

A free Postiz account at https://postiz.pro/inomsxbt

Everything below follows one example from start to finish, with the exact prompts, so you can copy them and get the same kind of result.

  1. Pick one slideshow format that already works

Don’t start from a blank page. A format that already works for someone else is a safer bet than an idea you made up at 11pm.

Here is how to find one:

  1. Open TikTok or Instagram and search “your niche + slideshow”, plus two or three close variants.

  2. Filter to the last 30 days

  3. Open the posts with the most views, then check the account. If it has under 50k followers and the post still did well, the format did the work, not the audience.

  4. Save 10 of these. Screenshot every slide of each one into a folder, one subfolder per post.

Then cut the list down with four questions:

  • Can you rebuild it without filming a person?
  • Is it 5 to 8 slides?
  • Is the hook on slide 1 plain text on an image?
  • Does the app only show up around slide 4 or 5, not slide 1?
    If a post fails any of those, skip it. Everything left is a candidate.

The running example for the rest of this guide is a made-up sleep tracking app called Nightly, and the format is “i tracked my sleep for 30 days, here is what changed”. Swap in your own app and format as you go.

  1. Teach Fable 5.2 your app: the app brief

If you skip this step, every slideshow will sound like it was written for a generic app. So write one document about your app, once and let Claude read it every time.

In Claude, create a Project called “UGC Slideshows” and paste the brief into the project instructions. Every new chat inside that project starts with the brief already loaded. Select Claude Fable 5.2 as the model.
The brief should be short and blunt. Use this template:

APP: [AppName] 
ONE LINE: [what it does in plain words, no marketing language] WHO IT IS FOR: [one specific person, e.g. “night-shift nurses who can’t switch off”] 
THE MOMENT: [the single moment a new user says “oh, that’s cool”] WHAT USERS COMPLAIN ABOUT BEFORE THEY FIND US: 

  • [complaint 1, in their words] 
  • [complaint 2] 
  • [complaint 3] 
    VOICE: [e.g. “talks like a friend texting, lowercase is fine, never says ‘game-changer’”] 
    NEVER SAY: [words and claims you will not use] 
    MY 5 BEST POSTS EVER (hook only):

 

  1. [hook] 
  2. [hook] 
    … 
    ASSETS: 8 screenshots in the folder /app-screens, named 01-home, 02-streak, etc.

The “never say” line matters more than it looks. Models like certain phrases and your audience can smell them. Add to that list every time a draft annoys you.
The fastest way to fill it in is to talk. Dictate five minutes about your app into your phone, paste the transcript into Claude, and ask Fable 5.2 to turn it into the template above. Then add one more instruction: “List everything you had to guess, as questions.” Answer those questions and the “THE MOMENT” line usually gets sharper.

  1. Tear the reference slideshow apart

Now give Fable 5.2 the reference slideshow from step 2. Open a new chat inside the project and attach every slide as an image, in order.
What you ask for matters most. A summary of the story is useless here. You want the format: the hook, the pacing, where the text sits, and where the app comes in. Use this prompt:

I’m attaching every slide of a slideshow I found on [TikTok or Instagram]. The slides are in order.
Do a teardown. Don’t summarise the story. I need the reusable format.
For each slide give me:

  1. The job of the slide (hook, setup, proof, turn, payoff, CTA) 2. The exact on-screen text, word for word
  2. Where the text sits (top, middle, bottom; left or centred),its size relative to the image, and whether it has an outline or a box
  3. What the image shows and how it is composed (subject, angle, lighting, crop)
  4. The emotion the viewer is meant to feel
    Then answer these:
  • What is the hook formula, as a fill-in-the-blank sentence? - What is the open loop that makes someone swipe?
  • On which slide does a product appear and how is it introduced? - Which three things must stay identical when I copy this, and which can change?
  • What would make this format stop working?
    Return the slide-by-slide part as a table and the rest as short bullets.

The last question is the one people skip. When Claude tells you what would break the format (too polished, a logo on slide 1, a sales line before slide.

  1. you get a list of things to check before you post.

Here is the kind of table that comes back, shown with the Nightly example. It illustrates the shape, so your real output will differ:

Read the whole thing before moving on. If it got something wrong, for example it called slide 3 “proof” when it is really the turn, say so in the chat and it will fix the table. That correction is what makes the next steps accurate.

  1. Write the slide script for your app

With the teardown and the app brief in the same chat, ask for the script. Use this prompt:

Using the teardown above and the app brief, write a slideshow for [AppName] in the same format. 

Rules: 

  • Same number of slides as the reference, and the same job for each slide. - Keep the hook formula. Change the topic to: [your topic]. 
  • Slide 1 text: under 10 words. Every other slide: under 18 words. - The app appears on slide [5], introduced the way the reference introduced its product. No sales line. 
  • Follow VOICE and NEVER SAY from the brief. 
  • If a number is needed, write [NUMBER] and I will fill it with a real one. Do not invent statistics. 
    For each slide return: 
  • slide number 
  • on-screen text 
  • an image prompt (vertical 9:16, phone-photo look, no text inside the image, same lighting and subject across all slides) 
  • which of my app screenshots to use, if any 
    Then give me: 
  • a caption under 150 characters and 3 hashtags 
  • 3 alternative slide 1 hooks, ranked by how closely they match the hook formula

Two lines in that prompt do a lot of work. 
“No text inside the image” keeps the image model from drawing broken letters. We add the text ourselves in step 6. 
“Same lighting and subject across all slides” is what makes six separate images look like one person’s camera roll instead of six stock photos.

Never post the first draft. Read every line out loud and rewrite anything you would not say to a friend. Give the hook the most attention: pick one of the three alternatives, then change a word or two so it sounds like you.

  1. Generate the slide images

Take the image prompts from the script and run them in your image generator. A few settings and habits keep the result looking like one camera roll.

Aspect ratio: 9:16, and 1080 x 1920 if the model lets you pick a size.

Slide 1 first. Generate it, pick the best of four, then attach it as a reference image when you generate slides 2 to 5. That is what keeps the person, room and lighting the same. 
One style block, reused. Paste the same sentence at the end of every image prompt, for example: “candid phone photo, natural window light, slightly imperfect framing, no filters, no text, no logos.” 
Never generate the app screen. Image models draw fake interfaces that look right from far away and wrong up close. For the slide where the app appears, use a real screenshot from your app screens folder. 
Generate 3 to 4 options per slide and keep the one that looks least like AI. Perfect skin and perfect symmetry are the giveaway.

This is the shape of one image prompt: 
A [age]-year-old [person description] sitting on a [location], looking at their phone with a tired but relieved expression. Candid phone photo, natural window light, slightly imperfect framing, no filters, no text, no logos. Vertical 9:16.

Before moving on, zoom in on every image and check hands, teeth, background text and anything that should be symmetrical. Expect to regenerate several slides. That is normal.

Six AI-generated images in one album. Image 5 is a stand-in screen from my phone Clock app.

  1. Add the text overlay

The text is added after the images, so it is always sharp and always spelled right. You can do this in Canva or CapCut. Both are free to start with and no code is needed.

  1. Create a custom design of 1080 x 1920 px (9:16).
  2. Upload your six images and put one on each page, scaled to fill the page.
  3. Add a text box to each page with the text from your script. Use a bold sans-serif font, centred.
  4. Set the size and position from the settings below.
  5. Style the first page’s text once, then copy that style to the other pages so every slide matches.
  6. Export all pages as JPG or PNG and check them in order.

Save the finished design as a template. For the variations in step 7, swap the images and the text and leave everything else alone.

The finished template in Canva: six pages, one text box per slide, with a shadow so the text stays readable.

The settings used here, and why:
Hook slide: 84px, centred. It has to be readable on a phone held at arm’s length. Other slides: 56 to 64px.
White text with a black outline of about size/14. It stays readable on bright and dark images alike.
Top margin 260px, bottom margin around 540px. The platform puts its own buttons and caption over the edges of the slide. Check these values against the in-app preview on your platform, since the layout changes now and then.
Max 18 characters per line on the hook, 24 on the rest. Short lines look native. Wide paragraphs look like an ad.

  1. Turn one winner into variations

Once a slideshow is posted and doing well, don’t start over. Go back to the same chat and ask for variations.

The prompt: This slideshow worked. Make 5 variations that keep the same mechanism and change the surface.
Keep: the hook formula, slide count, the job of each slide, the text length limits, and the app appearing on slide 5.
Change: the scenario, the person’s situation, the specific story, and the emotional angle. Use a different angle each time, from this list: relief, embarrassment, curiosity, frustration, pride.
Each variation must be different enough that someone who saw the first one would not feel they are watching a repeat.
Return the same format as before, plus a one-line “angle” label per variation so I can track which angle performs.

The angle label is the useful part. After a week you can see whether “embarrassment” posts beat “relief” posts, and that tells you what to ask for next.

Then repeat steps 5 and 6 for each variation. The first slideshow takes the longest. The five after it go fast because the brief, the teardown and the script are already in the chat.

  1. Schedule everything in Postiz

By now you have a set of finished slideshows in folders. This is where most people stall, because uploading, captioning and timing each one by hand eats the evening. Postiz handles that part.

The routine:

  1. Connect the accounts. Add each channel once in Postiz.

  2. Create a post per slideshow. Paste the caption and hashtags from the script, and pick the channel. Check in the editor that your platform’s slideshow or carousel format is offered for that channel.

  3. Pick the slot. Drag the post onto the calendar instead of typing times. One slideshow per account per day, and never two of the same format on the same day.

  4. Spread the variations. Put the five variations from step 7 on different days, ideally on different accounts, so the same hook is not in front of the same people twice in a row.

  5. Review the week. Open the calendar view and look for gaps, doubled-up days and any post with the wrong caption attached.

Here is an example:

Schedule the whole batch in one sitting, so for the rest of the week the only job left is replying to comments.

  1. Results: What the posts actually got

Scheduling the content was only half the experiment. The next step was seeing how the slideshows performed once they went live.

Here are the results from the six-post batch, including views and engagement across the posts.

The numbers give you something concrete to work with. Instead of guessing which hook or story worked, you can compare the posts and see which ones earned more views, saves and shares.

One batch is not enough to establish a winning formula, but it gives you a starting point for the next one.

  1. Read the numbers and feed them back

A week after posting, pull the analytics for every post and give them to Fable 5.2, in the same project, so it still has the brief and the teardown in context. Paste the numbers as a table (or attach screenshots) and use this prompt:

Here are the stats for last week’s [N] slideshows: views, likes, saves, shares, comments, and link clicks or installs where I have them. Each row also has its hook and its angle label.

Sort them into four groups:

  1. Winners: high views and high saves or shares
  2. Hooked but didn’t convert: high views, low saves and clicks 3. Quiet but loved: low views, high saves
  3. Flops

For each group, tell me what the hooks and angles have in common. Then write a failure log: for every flop, one sentence on the most likely reason, based only on the data I gave you. If the data can’t explain it, say so.

Finish with the brief for next week’s batch: which format, which angles, and which 3 hooks to test.

Two habits make this work:
Saves and shares matter more than likes. A save means somebody wants to come back to it.

Keep the failure log as a file and paste it into the project instructions. The next batch gets written knowing what already flopped. 

Then the loop starts again at step 2 with the winning format.

What you should still do yourself

The model does the typing. These parts should stay with you:

The app brief. Nobody knows the moment your app clicks better than you do. Reading every slide before it is scheduled. Wrong text, a seventh finger, a screenshot from the wrong screen. A quick review catches these, and they are expensive after posting.

Fact-checking any claim. If a slide states a number, the number has to be true. Fill any [NUMBER] placeholders yourself.

The hook. Claude gives you three options. Pick one and change the words until you would say it out loud.

Labeling AI content. Several platforms require you to mark AI-generated images. Turn that on every time and don’t try to hide it.

Replying to comments. Real replies from a real person.

The kill and scale calls. Fable 5.2 sorts the posts. You decide what gets cut and what gets five more variations.

It also does not always work. Some batches will do almost nothing. When that happens it is usually a weak hook or a format that has been copied too much, and the failure log is how you find out which.

The whole system in one recap

  1. Save 10 slideshows that already worked in your niche and pick one format.
  2. Write an app brief once and keep it in a Claude Project with Fable 5.2.
  3. Have Fable 5.2 tear the reference apart: hook formula, text placement, where the app appears.
  4. Have it write your script in that format, with a hook you rewrite yourself.
  5. Generate the images (9:16, no text inside, reuse slide 1 as the reference), and use real app screenshots.
  6. Add the text in Canva or CapCut with one saved template so every slide is consistent.
  7. Ask for five variations that keep the mechanism and change the angle. 8. Schedule the batch on a calendar in Postiz.
  8. Pull the numbers a week later, sort them, write the failure log, and start again

The scheduling step is the one most people drop, and it is the one that turns a good afternoon of work into a full week of posts. That is what Postiz is for. 

Try it: sign up at https://postiz.pro/inomsxbt, connect your accounts and schedule your first batch of slideshows.

entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @yaohongan2025（虹安） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

这篇文章只解决一个问题：构建你的搞钱思路

如果你问 2026 年普通人线上搞钱特征是什么，答案只有六个字：AI 轻资产中间商。

这一年，没有出现什么需要重资产投入的新物种，所有的爆发都集中在“信息差 + AI 工具交付”上。
最有说服力的数据来自闲鱼：仅 2026 年上半年，平台上的 AI 服务订单就狂飙到 981.6 万单（同比暴涨 157%），近 500 万人为 AI 技能掏了腰包。

很多人只看到了热闹，没看懂门道。Roland 我结合今年各平台的公开数据与一线观察，把 2026 年真正跑通的 5 大核心赚钱赛道逐一拆解，并按 1 月到 1 1 月的时间轴复盘了一遍全年的风口流转。还有 Roland 本人独家预测的 12 月份搞钱风口

建议先收藏，看懂别人的 2026年，才能提前卡位你的 2027年。

一、 2026 五大核心搞钱赛道深度拆解

今年所有的副业，几乎都跑不出以下 5 个赛道：

  1. AI 编程与建站接单（全年增速王：+1732%）
  • 怎么赚的钱：这是上半年增速最夸张的品类。过去做个企业官网、微信小程序或数据抓取脚本，没有几千上万块下不来；今年大量普通人靠着 Cursor、Claude、Gemini 等 AI 编程工具，直接去闲鱼接“低预算外包单”。
  • 商业逻辑：客户根本不在乎你是不是科班程序员，只在乎 300-500 块能不能明天交付一个能上线的页面。用 AI 写代码、用 Cloudflare/Vercel 免费托管，边际成本几乎为零，赚的是纯信息差和交付效率。
  • 壁垒与坑点：前期需求沟通极耗精力。高手会做成标准化模板，改改文案直接交付，把单均耗时压到 1 小时以内。
  1. AI 漫剧与短剧（流量与规模双爆：+1425%）
  • 怎么赚的钱：2026 年上半年，全网 AI 漫剧/短剧新上线超过 22 万部，用户规模直接干破 6 亿，前 5 个月市场规模就到了 220 亿左右。普通人的切入点主要有三个：
    一、直接做号吃分成/投流：比如 8 月份火出圈的算法工程师用 AI 做田园犬等宠物连续短剧，靠高完播率吃平台流量池。
    二、接定制代工单：帮短剧团队跑分镜、出图、转动态视频。
    三、卖教程与工作流（几乎 0 成本）：“教人怎么做短剧”稳赚不赔。有卖家半年光靠卖 AI 漫剧教程就卖出了 1.7 万份。
  • 壁垒与坑点：到了 10 月份，行业已经极度内卷，单部剧的爆款率跌到了千分之几。纯粹的“AI 换脸/粗糙洗稿”已经没流量了，现在拼的是剧本节奏、情绪张力，以及把国内爆款漫剧翻译出海。Roland本人也做了个出海短剧 APP 相关的网站，短剧这块未来 3 年都非常看好，直到 AI 视频成本完全打下来和 AI编剧质量有质的飞跃。
  1. AI 工作流部署与上门服务（年度现象级热潮）
  • 怎么赚的钱：开源 AI 智能体 OpenClaw（国内圈子里俗称“小龙虾”）从年初火到年中，连黄仁勋都将其称为“下一个 ChatGPT”。因为本地环境配置、API 接入、权限调试对普通小白极其不友好，直接催生了庞大的代安装/云部署服务——深圳等地甚至出现了排队装“小龙虾”的盛况，闲鱼上从几十块的远程调试到几百块的上门安装报价极其活跃。现在已经升级成为部署各种 DSH 相关的生意。
  • 商业逻辑：典型的“卖铲子”生意。90% 的小白依然卡在环境配置这一步，谁能提供“开箱即用”的交付，谁就能收割第一波红利。
  • 壁垒与坑点：生命周期短。随着阿里云、腾讯云等大厂陆续推出“一键部署”镜像，纯靠基础安装的利润迅速被压缩，下半年能继续赚钱的，都是做其他 AI 产品的部署服务，并且各自需求不同，很难批量做大。适合大学生兼职
  1. AI PPT 与办公代做（最稳的基本盘：+264%）
  • 怎么赚的钱：虽然增速不如编程和漫剧炸裂，但它是整个闲鱼 AI 服务里复购最稳、受众最广的品类（技能接单类整体占了平台 AI 订单的 45.1%）。学生答辩、体制内汇报、销售方案，全是刚需。
  • 商业逻辑：用 AI 大纲工具 + Gamma / 美图设计室 / Canva 可画等各类 AI PPT 插件快速生成初稿，人工花 15 分钟调一下排版和配色，一单收费 30–150 元。
  • 壁垒与坑点：纯拼手速和客服响应速度。非常适合时间碎片化的宝妈或兼职人群
  1. 海外平台创作者分成（X / Twitter 收益）
  • 真实情况：今年 9 月 X 平台调整了创作者激励计划。很多国内博主眼馋海外账号的阅读收益，涌入了一批有头有脸的国内中小 V，并且 Roland 估计会在明年有更大的爆发。一个原因是出海趋势不可阻挡，二是国内的自媒体从业者收入被各种渠道大砍，简直是抽骨吸髓，然后像 Roland 这种短时间内通过 X 拿到高收益，高商业影响力的例子会传到他们的耳朵里，谁听了不馋呢？
  • 但是与其花精力折腾风控极严的 X 创作者补贴，不如把 X 当成纯粹的引流入口，后端用独立站 AdSense、Affiliate（联盟佣金）或卖数字产品变现，这才是真正可控的美元现金流。Roland 这次又在以身作则了，自己就在做 AFF 相关的社群还有出海相关的生态构建，这块重点看好！！你们也可以私信我申请加入 AFF 联盟营销产品群。

二、 2026 全年 1–11 月副业风口时间轴复盘

把上面的赛道放进时间线里，你能清晰看到这一年钱是如何流动的：

  • 1 月（开年铺垫）：闲鱼 AI 技能服务率先起量，AI 绘画、朋友圈文案、基础表格处理成为第一批跑通的品类，全年“AI 消费”基调就此定下。
  • 2 月（内容井喷）：春节前后短视频消费爆发，AI 漫剧、AI 短剧在抖音、红果等平台供给与播放量双双暴增，第一批吃螃蟹的创作者开始批量起号。
  • 3 月（全民养虾）：OpenClaw（小龙虾）彻底引爆开发者与极客圈，地方政策与云厂商纷纷跟进。闲鱼远程部署、同城上门“装虾”订单迎来全年最高峰。
  • 4 月（技术平权）：AI 编程工具进一步普及，大量非技术背景的卖家涌入闲鱼接建站、插件、小工具外包单，推动该品类上半年同比暴涨 1732%。
  • 5 月（卖水人收割）：做剧的人多了，想学做剧的人更多。AI 漫剧教程、提示词模板、工作流打包销售迎来爆发，头部卖家单链接销量破万。
  • 6 月（年中大考与刚需）：毕业季 + 年中汇报季叠加，AI PPT 与办公代做需求激增；与此同时，全网 AI 短剧用户规模正式突破 6 亿大关。
  • 7 月（数据引爆入场）：7 月 29 日，闲鱼官方正式披露上半年 981.6 万单 AI 订单数据。各大科技媒体刷屏报道，吸引大批观望者下场，平台进入存量博弈期。
  • 8 月（垂直题材突围）：通用短剧开始审美疲劳，垂直细分题材跑出黑马——例如技术博主用 AI 制作的“中华田园犬”等宠物连续短剧拿下现象级播放；同时各大云厂商的小龙虾一键部署方案上线，安装服务向深度定制转型。
  • 9 月（海外规则洗牌）：9 月 8 日 X 平台正式切换新创作者奖励计划，大陆账号直接分成彻底受限，大批做海外内容的人开始转向“独立站 + SEO + 联盟营销”。
  • 10 月（精品化与出海）：国内 AI 短剧/漫剧爆款率降至千分之几，低质内容全面失灵，头部团队开始转向精品化制作和海外分发；Grok bot 自动化项目开始普及。
  • 11 月（AI 交付升级）：单纯在闲鱼卖“几百条 Prompt 提示词”彻底卖不动了，平台上的 AI 副业进入“交付封装期”。真正还在稳定出单的，都是把 AI 能力封装成开箱即用的工作流、自动化脚本或垂直行业模板（比如一键批量生成短视频工作流、定制化 Agent 配置包）等等。
  • 12 月（Roland 个人预测）： 明年可能是很多人的“职场最后一年”。大厂的离职潮与 AI 带来的组织瘦身，会迫使大批人提前筹备单人创业。脱离公司庇护后，个体对实战信息差和同行反馈的渴求会达到顶峰——垂直领域的实战型付费社群，即将迎来一次大爆发。单打独斗的时代过去了，未来会是付费圈子，甚至是高门槛付费圈子的天下。因为只有高门槛才能筑起信息壁垒，才能稳住自己的先发优势。

三、 写给想入局者的 3 条大实话

复盘完 2026 年的副业图谱，有三个结论我想直接甩出来：

  1. 别信“躺赚”，月入几百到几千才是常态：闲鱼官方给出的“卖家月均成交额 897 元”可太真实了，AI 副业的本质是用工具把你的业余时间折现，它能帮你赚出房租、伙食费甚至一台顶配电脑，但想靠它财务自由，必须把“接单服务”升级成“标准化数字产品”或“自动化流量站”。
  2. 永远做“卖铲子”的人，别去卷最红海的 C 端：做 AI 漫剧的爆款率只有千分之几，但卖漫剧工作流和教程的人赚得盆满钵满；折腾自动化配置的人头发掉了一地，但帮人上门安装调试的人按单收钱。哪里有焦虑和门槛，哪里就有交付生意。
  3. 单一平台红利期只有 3–6 个月：从 3 月的小龙虾安装，到 10 月的 AI 短剧内卷，每一个细分子风口的窗口期都在缩短，唯有圈子能长久。

2027 搞钱生存预测：普通人的 4 条出路

最后这部分，我把我对明年（2027 年）整个搞钱环境的 4 个核心判断直接摊开讲。看懂这四点，能帮你少走至少半年弯路：

1. 职场安全感彻底归零，“单人公司”成为标配

2026 年的 AI 只是帮你写写代码、改改 PPT；到了 2027 年，随着 Agent 自动化工作流的成熟，企业会发现过去 5 个人的部门，现在 1 个熟练使用 AI 的人就能扛下来。大厂的薪资收缩和优化潮不会停，明年很可能是很多普通打工人的“职场最后一年”。与其被动等裁员大礼包，不如从今年年底开始，用下班时间跑通一个能产生现金流的“单人副业 MVP”。

2. “纯搬运/洗稿套壳”全面死亡，唯“信息增量”与“垂直交付”永生

无论是在国内闲鱼卖几百条泛泛的 Prompt，还是在海外做 AI 批量洗稿的 SEO 垃圾站，2027 年都会被平台算法和用户彻底淘汰。未来的流量和溢价只流向两个地方：

  • 有独家“信息增量”的内容与工具（AI 搜索引擎和用户只愿意为真实数据、实测体验、垂直痛点买单）；
  • 重度封装的交付结果（别卖半成品工具，直接卖能帮客户省时间、赚到钱的最终方案）。

3. 国内卷存量，海外赚增量——出海依然是普通人最大的杠杆

国内各行各业都在缩量内卷，自媒体分成砍到骨子里，接单价格战打到地板上。而海外市场（尤其是北美和欧洲）不仅客单价是国内的 5–7 倍，而且用户有极强的为软件、工具、订阅制内容付费的习惯。2027 年，“用国内的 AI 工程效率 + 海外的商业化变现渠道（独立站 / App / 联盟营销）”，依然是普通人能撬动的最大财富杠杆。

4. 单打独斗彻底失效，高门槛的“实战小圈子”成为核心壁垒

当 AI 把写代码、做内容、建站的门槛全部拉平之后，“知道做什么（信息差）”和“踩过哪些坑（试错成本）”成了唯一稀缺的资源。2027 年，闭门造车的单人创业者会死得非常快，而聚集了一群有真实产出、互相交换流量和实战打法的高门槛付费圈子，将成为普通人抱团抗风险的标配。

Roland 今年没什么别的愿望，就想成为出海搞钱赛道里的头部风向标。

我的长文全部免费，希望能做到既帮你省钱，也帮你赚钱。2027 年，别盲目全盘照抄我的打法（每个人的资源储备和认知不同，很难直接复制），但你可以在我后续推荐的搞钱路线里，挑出 3–5 条死磕尝试——只要跑通一条，明年你就赢过 95% 的人了。

entry.title: 万字干货｜Gemini 4 + Antigravity，从 0 到 1 跑通全自动出片（附 Agent 指令）
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @xueyu1125（雪瑜） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

很多人不知道：Antigravity 其实不能生成视频。

上一篇我写它能把爆款视频的提示词反推出来，文末吐槽了一句：谷歌全家桶，就差出片这最后一块。

这两天我把这块接上了。

现在同一个对话里，它看完参考视频、画好角色定妆照、写完提示词，直接调视频模型出片，再下载、配回原声、抽帧给我验收。我只管花钱前点头和最后看片。

一共跑通三条路，前两条用的全是 Google AI 会员本来就送的额度。 Pro、Ultra 5x、Ultra 20x 都能用。

我自己是 Pro 会员，下文的额度和账单都按 Pro 实测；Ultra 的额度更多，方法完全一样。

每节末尾都有一段指令，复制给 Antigravity 就能跑。

小目录

  • 一、Antigravity 缺的那一块：看得懂，出不了片
  • 二、你的会员里，藏着两份出片额度
  • 三、第一条路 · Gemini API：用会员赠金后台直出
  • 四、第二条路 · Google Flow：用深度灰模过审，花会员点数
  • 五、第三条路 · 外部视频命令行：LibTV、即梦、小云雀都能接
  • 六、Pro 够不够用：我的真实账单
  • 写在最后

───

一、Antigravity 缺的那一块：看得懂，出不了片

先交代前情。上一篇讲的是：刷到一条爆款视频，作者不给提示词，就丢给 Antigravity 让它看，它能把镜头、运镜、节奏反推成提示词。

能反推，是因为 Antigravity 的大脑是 Gemini。GPT、Claude 看视频是抽帧看截图，Gemini 是真的看懂了动作和节奏。 现在换成 Gemini 4，看片这一步更稳。

但那篇写完我很别扭：前面看片、反推、画定妆照，它全能干；一到出片，我还得自己打开网页、传图、点生成、等、下载，再丢回给它检查。

最麻烦的不是点几下鼠标，是闭环断了。

它看不到成片，就没法对着原片挑错、改提示词、再跑一版。来回搬运一次，我就得在场一次。

接上以后，分工变成这样：

  • 我：说清要做什么片子，花钱前点头，看样片，拍板。
  • Antigravity：看原片、定角色、写提示词、选通道、提交、下载、配回原声、抽帧和原片并排对比，不合格自己改一版再交。

这篇讲的就是”出片”这一块，怎么接。

───

二、你的会员里，藏着两份出片额度

很多人订了 Google AI Pro 或 Ultra，只拿来在网页上聊天。其实会员里有两份能出视频的额度，跟 Antigravity 一拍即合。

第一份：Gemini API 赠金（美元）。

今年起，Google 把开发者计划的福利并进了 AI 会员，每个月送一笔 Google Cloud 赠金，可以拿来调 Gemini API，包括视频模型。按 Google 开发者计划的官方 FAQ：

  • Pro：每月 10 美元
  • Ultra 5x：每月 40 美元
  • Ultra 20x：每月 100 美元

赠金要自己去领，领了才有；每笔有效期一年。第三节有图文步骤。

第二份：Google Flow 点数。

Google Flow 是谷歌官方的 AI 视频创作网页（flow.google.com）。你可以把它理解成谷歌版的即梦：传图、传视频、写一句话，它帮你出视频。

会员每个月送 Flow 点数，Pro 是 1000 点，Ultra 多得多。出视频按点数扣，生图基本不扣。

顺手把几个会反复出现的名字讲清楚：

  • Omni、Veo：谷歌的两个视频模型系列。Omni 擅长”看着参考视频和参考图来生成”，这篇主要用它（Omni 1.2 Flash）；Veo 偏电影感画质。
  • Nano Banana 2（Flow 里简称 Nano 2）：谷歌的生图模型，就是网上很火那个”香蕉”。在 Flow 里用它画角色图，实测不扣点数。
  • Antigravity：谷歌官方的命令行 AI Agent，大脑是 Gemini。能读文件、跑命令、开浏览器，这篇里它是总导演。

三条路，一句话说清区别：

  • Gemini API：吃赠金，纯后台跑，最省心；参考视频最长 10 秒。
  • Google Flow：吃点数，能直接喂 15 秒参考视频；但它没有接口，得让 Agent 操作网页，审核也严。
  • 外部视频命令行：吃第三方平台的积分；谷歌这两条卡住时兜底，长镜头、多人复杂场面更稳。

───

三、第一条路 · Gemini API：用会员赠金后台直出

原理：Agent 直接给谷歌的视频模型发请求

API 就是程序之间的”窗口”。Antigravity 把”参考视频 + 角色图 + 提示词”打包发给谷歌的视频模型，模型在云端生成，Antigravity 每隔一会儿去问一次好了没，好了就下载。

全程不开网页、不占你的屏幕。 这是三条路里最像”全自动”的一条。

实操第 1 步：把会员赠金领出来

打开 Google AI Studio（aistudio.google.com），左下角有「领取免费 API 赠金」的卡片，点进去。

会直接弹出领取窗口，选好结算账号，点「兑换并继续」。Ultra 会员这里显示的金额更高。

领完以后，在 Google Cloud 的「结算 → 赠金」页能看到一行 Google Developer Program premium benefit、状态「可用」，就是领到了。

实操第 2 步：先预充 5 美元，赠金才用得上

我领完赠金去调接口，AI Studio 结算页弹了一条黄色提示：此账号已转为预付款结算方式，余额需大于 0 美元方可恢复服务，符合条件的 GCP 赠金会优先抵扣。

这一步很多人会卡住： 赠金领到了，接口还是调不通。我是先预充了最低的 5 美元，服务才恢复。充完以后，调用费用会优先从赠金里扣。

实操第 3 步：拿 API 密钥，交给 Antigravity

在 AI Studio 左侧「API 密钥」里新建一把密钥，选你刚绑定赠金的那个项目。

密钥别直接贴进对话里。 存成本机的一个文件（比如 ~/.config/video-gen/.env，权限设成只有自己能读），然后告诉 Antigravity 文件在哪。

使用边界：这 4 条踩过才知道

① 参考视频最长 10 秒。

模型能输出 15 秒，但你喂给它当参考的原视频，超过 10 秒直接被退回。

想复刻 15 秒的片子，就切成两段（比如 0-8 秒、7-15 秒）分别跑，再拼起来。拼接处人物衣服、站位可能对不上，后面 Tips 里说怎么防。

② 参考视频要先去掉声音。

带音轨的视频传上去，秒拒，连原因都不细说。先把声音去掉再传，出片以后再把原视频的音乐配回去。这两步 Antigravity 用 ffmpeg 一句命令就能做。

③ 参考视频不能比你要的成片短。

你要 8 秒成片，参考视频就得 ≥ 8 秒，哪怕短 0.5 秒也会被拒。剪的时候多留 0.1-0.2 秒最稳。

④ 不说分辨率，它默认给你 720p，很贵。

我第一次没注意，两条 9.5 秒的 720p 直接花掉 3.16 美元，一条 1.58。Pro 一个月才 10 美元。

先用 360p 试，构图、动作都对了再出高清。

Tips：提示词怎么写，换角色才不乱

  • 按衣服认人，别按位置认人。 多人舞台一换位，”左一换成 A、左二换成 B”必乱。要写”穿黑袖白衬衣的那位换成 A”，模型会跟着衣服追。
  • 告诉它角色图只管长相。 角色定妆照一般是站着摆拍，不说清楚，成片里人物会照着定妆照的姿势站桩。加一句”角色图只锁长相和服装，动作完全照原片”。
  • 背景要锁死。 不写的话，模型会把定妆照里的背景搬进来。写清”保留原片的舞台、灯光和机位，只换台上的人”。
  • 提示词短一点反而好。 我堆过一大串”必须、严禁”，结果请求直接校验失败；删到简洁清楚，一次过，动作还更自然。
  • 出片后要抽帧对比。 让 Antigravity 从原片和成片各抽 6 帧拼成一张图并排看，比你自己拖进度条快得多。

一键甩给 Antigravity

───

四、第二条路 · Google Flow：用深度灰模过审，花会员点数

原理：Flow 能干活，但它没有门

Flow 有三个 API 没有的好处：

  • 能直接喂 15 秒参考视频，不用切段；
  • 扣的是会员点数，不花赠金；
  • 出片后下载时可以 5 点升到 1080p，比重新生成高清便宜得多。

在 Flow 里，Omni 1.2 Flash 出一条 15 秒：360p 是 20 点，720p 是 60 点。下面这张是我开着 720p、一次出 2 条时的报价。

问题是：Flow 是给人用的网页，没有给程序用的接口。 Agent 想用它，只能像人一样去操作网页。这里有三道坎：

  • 没有官方接口，只能模拟浏览器操作；
  • 有人机验证，谷歌会拦”一看就是机器”的无头浏览器，必须是真的 Chrome 窗口；
  • 上传文件走的是系统原生的选文件窗口，脚本点不进去，本地视频传不上去。

两种接法，各有千秋

接法一：开源工具 gflow-cli。

有人把 Flow 网页背后的接口包成了命令行，还自带 MCP（让 Agent 直接调用的插件接口）：

https://github.com/ffroliva/gflow-cli

  • 好处：一句命令就能生图、生视频、查点数，几乎不费 Agent 的算力；
  • 不足：只能传图片，不能传参考视频；默认只下载 360p；每次会弹出一个独立的 Chrome 窗口抢你屏幕（我写了个小脚本让它自动最小化）；
  • 风险：它是非官方的，调的是谷歌的内部接口，谷歌随时可能改，账号风险自担。

接法二：web-access 这类浏览器 skill。

让 Antigravity 直接接管你日常那个已登录 Google 的 Chrome，像人一样点按钮。

  • 好处：网页上能点的它都能点，挂视频、切分辨率、点 720p 下载都行；
  • 不足：每一步都要看页面、截图、判断，非常费算力，也慢；参考视频第一次进项目，还是要你手动拖一下（就是上面说的那个系统选文件窗口）。

我的组合： 生图、注入角色图、查点数这种轻活交给 gflow；挂参考视频、提交、下载 720p 这几步交给浏览器 skill。你只需要在开头拖一次视频。

最大的坎：真人视频过不了审

我第一次直接把女团的打歌原片拖进去，进度跑到 83%，卡片直接消失了。另一条连卡片都没出。没报错，也没扣点。

Flow 对真人脸和有版权的画面审核很严，会在后台静默取消。

解法是深度灰模。

深度灰模（行业里叫深度图，Depth Map）就是把彩色视频洗成”离镜头近的发白、远的发黑”的灰色剪影：五官、衣服花纹、台标全没了，只剩人在哪、怎么动、镜头怎么推拉。

审核看不到真人和版权内容，就放行了；模型照样能读出站位和运镜。我两条 15 秒都是一次出片。

实操步骤

① 本地把原片转成深度灰模。

让 Antigravity 用开源的 Depth-Anything-V2 模型转。本地跑不用钱，就是慢：15 秒 720p 的视频，我这台老 Mac 用 CPU 跑了 20 分钟左右。

② 在 Flow 里新建项目，把灰模视频拖进去。

这是全流程唯一要你动手的一步。

③ 让 Agent 把角色图注入同一个项目。

用 gflow 调 Nano Banana 2，把角色定妆照传进同一个项目。第一次传图，Flow 会弹一个”确认你有权使用这张图”的窗口，你在网页上点一次确认就行。

④ 让 Agent 挂素材、提交。

点输入框左边的「+」，先切到「视频」标签挂灰模，再切「图片」标签勾角色图，写提示词，提交。

⑤ 出片后下载，配回原声。

满意的那条，下载时选 1080p，多花 5 点。

使用边界

  • 深度灰模丢掉了表情和手指这些细节。 适合”同构图、同节奏”的二创；要逐帧 1:1 复刻舞蹈，不如第一条路。
  • 只能放在会员点数够的时候用。 点数用完，这条路就停了，下个月再来。
  • gflow 是非官方工具。 谷歌改版它就可能失灵，别把它当唯一的路。

Tips：省点数、少翻车

  • 提交前看一眼底部是不是”15 秒”。 「+」弹窗默认停在”全部/最近”，新生成的图片会把视频顶下去。我就因为这个，一次本该挂视频的任务按 8 秒纯图提交了，白扣了点数。
  • 别同时挂”多人合成的同框图”。 猫那条我多挂了一张正面合成图，结果镜头全程正面单机位，原片的切镜没了。只挂灰模 + 单人角色图。
  • 先 360p 试动作。 20 点一条，动作对了再出 720p，或者直接下载时升 1080p。
  • 生图尽量放在 Flow 里做。 Nano Banana 2 生图实测不扣点。

一键甩给 Antigravity

───

五、第三条路 · 外部视频命令行：LibTV、即梦、小云雀都能接

原理：给 Agent 插一个新插头

谷歌两条路各有卡点：API 参考视频只能 10 秒，Flow 审核严。碰到 15 秒以上的长镜头、四五个人来回换位的复杂场面，我就换第三方平台。

现在很多视频平台都出了命令行工具（CLI）或 MCP，本来就是给 Agent 用的。Antigravity 会跑命令，你把文档丢给它，它自己就能学会怎么用。

这条路不挑平台。 我恰好有 LibTV 的积分，所以拿它举例；你手里有哪家的积分，就接哪家。

能接哪些？文档在哪

  • LibTV：官方命令行 libtv；平台内 CLI 文档；装好后 libtv –help
  • 即梦（海外版 Dreamina）：官方命令行 dreamina；dreamina.capcut.com/tools/dreamina-cli
  • 小云雀（剪映出品）：命令行 pippit-tool-cli；npm 包 @pippit-dev/cli
  • MiniMax 海螺：官方 MCP；github.com/MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-MCP
  • 可灵：官方开放平台 API（MCP 目前是社区版）；可灵开放平台开发者文档

同一个平台里，通常还能选不同模型。LibTV 里就有 Seedance 2.5、Seedance 2.0、Wan 3.0 等好几个。

模型没有绝对的好坏，看任务。 我这个”四个虚拟角色换掉女团成员”的任务：

  • Seedance 2.5：25 秒一条，四个角色从头到尾不串、不变形，节奏稳。这个任务里最强。
  • Wan 3.0：15 秒，很多原片真人没被换掉，还留在画面里。

换个简单点的任务，结论可能不一样。

实操步骤（以 LibTV 为例）

① 登录。 让 Antigravity 跑 libtv login web，在弹出的网页里登录一次，之后它就能一直用。

② 建画布、传素材。 它会建一张画布，把参考视频（先把角落台标糊掉）和角色图传上去。

③ 选”混合参考”模式出片。 参考视频 + 角色图一起连到生成节点，记得打开声音，先出 480p 看效果。

④ 满意再升清。 在 LibTV 画布里选中那条，点高清重塑就行，这一步我自己在网页上点。

使用边界

  • 花的是第三方的积分，不是谷歌会员权益。 Seedance 2.5 480p 一条 25 秒，大约 500 积分，不便宜。
  • 每个模型时长上限不同。 Seedance 2.5 单条最长 30 秒；Wan 3.0 混合参考最长 15 秒，超了会失败退积分。
  • 文档以 –help 为准。 平台更新很快，网上的教程可能已经过时。

Tips：长片怎么接得上

尾帧续写。 积分不够一次跑完、或者想往后接一段，就把上一段成片的最后一帧截下来当参考图，连同原片接下来那段一起喂进去，再出 10 秒。

我用这个办法把 25 秒接到了 34.5 秒，衣服、光影、站位都接上了，拼起来看不出接缝。

声音别关。 为了省积分把声音关掉，成片没声音就废了一半。降成本只降分辨率和时长。

一键甩给 Antigravity

───

六、Pro 够不够用：我的真实账单

先说结论：跑通流程，Pro 够；拿来量产，Pro 不够。

这两天我只做了两个复刻任务（一个女团舞台、一个猫咪短片），来回调了十几版。账单是这样的：

Gemini API 赠金：10 美元，折腾完这一轮只剩 3.95 美元。

  • 大头是一开始没设分辨率，两条 720p 就花了 3.16 美元；
  • 后面全改 360p 试，花得慢多了，但来回十几版，还是花掉了一大半；
  • 另外，账单有延迟：Agent 当时查到的余额比实际多，别全信实时数字，隔天再看一眼；
  • 按 720p 一条 1.58 美元算，10 美元就是 6 条左右。拿来调试够，拿来出成片很紧。

Flow 点数：从 1047 点用到 779 点，用掉 268 点。

  • 15 秒 720p 一条 60 点，1000 点满打满算 16 条；
  • 360p 一条 20 点，能跑 50 条，但 360p 只能看动作，不能发；
  • 还有一次因为没挂上视频白扣的点数，前面 Tips 里说过。

第三方积分：Seedance 2.5 一条 25 秒 480p，约 500 积分。

  • 效果最好，也最贵；我的积分跑完 25 秒、20 秒、10 秒三条，就剩 400 多了，还得留着做高清。

所以我的判断：

  • 想先把流程跑通、偶尔做一两条好玩的：Pro 足够，Antigravity 自带的出片能力就都有了；
  • 想拿它日更、起号：Pro 的额度撑不住。同样的方法，Ultra 5x 每月 40 美元赠金、Ultra 20x 每月 100 美元，Flow 点数也多得多。

说实话，跑完这一轮，我自己都想升 Ultra 了。

想升 Ultra 5x 的，可以看 @xueyu1125 这篇，订阅步骤写得很清楚：

───

写在最后

上一篇结尾我说，谷歌全家桶就差出片这一块。

现在这块补上了：Gemini 4 负责看懂视频，Antigravity 负责调度，三条出片通道负责干活。 赠金、Flow 点数、第三方积分，哪个先用完就切下一条。

如果你也是 Google 会员，会员里的出片额度大概率还没领。照着第三节领出来，把上面三段指令甩给 Antigravity，今晚就能出第一条。

觉得有用，欢迎转发给同样订了 Google 会员的朋友 🙏

entry.title: 本地大模型：数字人案例实测教程
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @EianLu（Eian） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

你一定有这样的烦恼：

想拍口播，觉得自己人也不好看，声音也不好听，鼓起勇气去化妆、打光、半天整了一条视频出去0 个赞。

于是就想偷懒用数字人：

视频是出来了，发现一条视频花了几十块，效果差强人意，重试一下又是几十块，发出去还没流量。

有没有低成本效果又逼真的方法？

不知道，试试就知道了。

本地显卡实测：

先看结论

案例一：

只有一张照片，能让它开口吗？

能。

给它一张我的半身照、一段 10 秒的配音，它会从零开始把整段视频画出来，人会眨眼、点头、比手势，嘴跟着声音动。

在Dgx Spark 上，10 秒的视频大约等 8 分半钟。

第一次跑出来效果还行，但很快就翻车了：人物动不动把两只大手怼到镜头前，挡住半个画面。

问题出在提示词：我写了”近距离自拍、双手做各种自然手势”，AI 就真的把手往镜头上举。 改成”镜头不动、保持照片原来的距离、手放低”以后，这个问题就没了。

下图是同一张照片、同一句话，旧描述和新描述的对比：

这里有个小白很容易忽略的点： AI 很听话，你写什么它就放大什么。

我还试过写”一步一步讲解教程”，结果人物全程只用一根手指点来点去；

改成”像跟朋友聊天，摊开手掌、偶尔把手放下”，动作马上自然了。

还有两件事要提前知道：

第一，偶尔嘴会噘成一个”O”形，换句子、改描述都压不下去，我到现在也没找到原因。

第二，同样的设置跑两次，结果可能完全不同，我跑过 3 次，有一次整个场景莫名其妙从晚上变成了白天。

AI 生成带运气成分，正式出片最好多跑几条，挑最好的一条，并且从头到尾看一遍再发。

案例二：手上有自己说话的视频，效果能更好吗

能，有两种用法。

**第一种，给 AI 当参考。 **

照片之外，再给 H3 一段十几秒的自己说话的视频，让它更认识你。

我用人脸识别软件给成片打”像不像本人”的分，满分 1：只给照片是 0.900，加了参考视频变成 0.948，低头的角度也和真人一样了。代价是慢，10 秒要等 23 分钟左右，差不多是只用照片的 3 倍。

第二种，只换嘴。

这就是”对口型”：原视频一帧不动，只把嘴巴那一小块重新画，让它跟着新的声音动。我用的是字节开源的 LatentSync。

除了嘴全是真的，所以它是几种里最真实的，也最快，10 秒只要 3 分半。

缺点是动作全是原视频里的，你原来在搓手，成片里还在搓手。

下图是同一段素材用四种跑法生成的截图。

给小白的建议：

如果你本来就有一段对着镜头说话的视频，先试对口型，最容易出效果。

拍的时候注意正脸、嘴别被挡、头别大幅转动，视频最好比要说的话长一点。

案例三：美团新出的模型，比 H3 强吗

11 月 15 日，美团开源了数字人模型 LongCat，也是照片加声音出视频。

我用同一张照片、同一段声音，和 H3 正面比了一次；

怕只拿我一个人不公平，又用 AI 生成了一张虚构女性的照片（现实中没有这个人），配上合成女声再比一组。

结果是长相打平。像本人的分数两边只差 0.005 到 0.02，画面都很稳，衣服和背景全程没有变形。

H3 表情更活泼，嘴张得更大；LongCat 动作收一点，会自然眨眼。

差距在速度。同样 10 秒，H3 要 8 分半；

LongCat 低清版要 26 分钟，清晰度接近 H3 的版本要 71 分钟。

为什么差这么多？

主要是”步数”不一样。LongCat 每段要算 8 遍，10 秒还得分 3 段接着生成，一共算 24 遍；H3 我优化过一次出完，只要 4 遍。

那 LongCat 有什么用？它能一段接一段往后生成，官方说能做 10 分钟以上的长视频；H3 一次最多十几秒，长了得自己拼接。

想做一镜到底的长口播，可以考虑LongCat。

科普一：想在自己电脑上跑，需要什么硬件

先记住一条最朴素的规律：模型要整个装进”工作台”才能干活。

这个工作台，普通电脑上是显卡自带的内存，叫显存；

DGX Spark 这类机器上是 CPU 和显卡共用的一大块内存，叫统一内存。

模型文件有多大，工作台至少就得有多大，真正算起来还要再多占一大块。

工作台放不下，程序会直接报错退出，大家管这个叫”爆显存”。

那为什么一个数字人要下载好几个模型文件？

因为它是好几个小模型一起干活。

主模型负责画画面，是最大的那个；

文本编码器负责读懂你写的描述；

VAE 负责把画面压缩成 AI 好处理的小数据，最后再还原成正常的图片；还有专门处理声音的部分，让嘴型跟上声音。

H3 要下载的五个文件，就是主模型、加速补丁、文本编码器、画面 VAE 和声音 VAE。

下面是我实测的三个模型的”体重”：

对照这张表，常见的几档机器大概是这样：

16 GB 显存的游戏显卡，比如 RTX 5070 Ti。

我实测 H3 做 6 秒以内的短片能跑，开了加速以后，一个 6 秒左右的任务只要 492 秒，比 Spark 的 807 秒还快。但做到 12 秒就爆显存。

24 到 32 GB 显存的高端显卡，比如 RTX 4090、5090。

这一档我手上没有，没实测。按文件大小看，H3 主模型 34 GB 就已经比显存大了，能不能跑、能跑多长，要看软件能不能把模型分批搬进显卡，我没验证过，买之前最好先找有这张卡的人实测。

**大内存一体机，比如我用的 NVIDIA DGX Spark，121 GB 统一内存。**三个模型都能跑，H3 能做到 15 秒，LongCat 能跑 720p。

缺点有两个：它是 ARM 芯片，很多 AI 软件是按x86 架构写的，我装对口型就踩了十来个坑；而且单论短片段的速度，它还比不过 5070 Ti。

选型建议：先想清楚要做什么。只想体验一下，做 5 秒左右的短片段，16 GB 显卡就够；想做 10 到 15 秒的正式口播，或者想试美团这类新模型，得有 100 GB 以上的显存或统一内存。

另外，我测的这几个模型都是cuda 生态的，其他牌子的显卡我没试过。如果一个月只做几条，用云端算力显卡按分钟付费可能更划算。

科普二：看懂渲染设置里的那些词

打开 ComfyUI 这类工具，会看到一堆设置项，了解下基础概念：

**步数（steps）：**擦雪花的遍数，就是”4 步””8 步””20 步”里说的步。有点像画画，先打草稿，再一遍遍修细节。每多一步，就要把整段视频从头到尾再算一遍，所以耗时基本跟步数成正比。

**种子（seed）：**那屏雪花点最开始长什么样，由一个编号决定，这个编号就是种子。其他设置都不变时，种子一样，结果就一样；

换个种子，相当于重新抽一次签。我用同样的设置换了 3 个种子，有一条整个场景从晚上变成了白天。所以正式出片多换几个种子，挑最好的一条。

**LoRA：**给主模型挂的小补丁。主模型动辄几十 GB，重新训练一遍成本很高；LoRA 只有几个 GB，挂上去就能让模型多一项本事，取下来模型还是原样。H3 的主模型 34 GB，我挂的加速 LoRA 只有 1.96 GB。

LoRA 一般有个”强度”设置，1.0 是满强度，数字越小影响越弱。我还试过一个让画面更锐利的 LoRA，开到 0.3，像本人的分数没涨反而掉了一点，所以补丁不是挂得越多越好。

**turbo、蒸馏、加速版：**这类模型原本要二三十步甚至更多才能画清楚。有人专门把它训练成”几步就能画完”的快速版，这个过程叫蒸馏，名字里常带 turbo、distill 这类词，通常以 LoRA 的形式发布。

H3 挂上 turbo LoRA 后只要 4 步；美团 LongCat 自带两个这样的加速 LoRA，把步数压到 8 步。

**采样器（sampler）：**决定每一步具体怎么擦的算法，名字五花八门，比如我用的 res_multistep。新手直接用模板里的默认值就行，一般不用动。

**提示词和负面提示词：**提示词写你想要什么，比如”镜头不动、手放低”；负面提示词写你不想要什么，比如”字幕、模糊、多余的手指”。

美团 LongCat 的代码里就内置了一长串负面提示词。前面案例一已经说过，AI 很听话，你写什么它就放大什么。

**分辨率、帧数、帧率：**分辨率是画面有多少个像素点，768×1344 就是宽 768、高 1344；480p、720p 说的是画面短的那条边大约 480、720 个点。帧率是每秒放多少张图，H3 是每秒 24 张，所以 10 秒要 243 帧。H3 对帧数还有个硬要求，必须是 17 的倍数再加 5。分辨率越高越慢，H3 做 1088×1920 的 10 秒视频要 128 分钟，是 768×1344 的 5 倍多。

**精度：BF16、INT8 和量化。**模型里存着几十亿个数字。BF16 每个数字记得更精细，文件也大；INT8 记得粗一点，文件小一半左右，效果通常差不多。把模型压成 INT8 这类小版本，就叫量化。显存不够时，先找量化版。我用的 H3 就是 INT8 版；还试过 66 GB 的 BF16 版，反而出了金色悬浮字、唇色发紫这些问题。

**注意力加速：Sage、flash-attn。**模型画画时，画面的每个部分都要和其他部分对一对，这一步叫”注意力”，是最费时间的环节。Sage 和 flash-attn 都是专门让这一步算得更快的插件。

我给 H3 开了 Sage，快了 22% 到 35%，画面肉眼看不出差别。美团 LongCat 官方用的是 flash-attn，但它在 Spark 的 ARM 芯片上装不上，我只好换成 PyTorch 自带的算法，结果一样，就是慢。

费用怎么算：

要花多少钱？

在自己机器上跑，电费几乎可以忽略，我估算一条 10 秒视频 1 分钱左右（按整机 100 瓦估算，没有用插座实测）。

作为对比，火山引擎即梦的数字人接口官方价是每秒 1 元，10 秒就是 10 元。本地跑真正的成本是机器本身和你等待的时间。

能用别人的照片吗？

破甲模型可以，不然我那么多换脸视频咋做的，当然注意侵权。

你该怎么使用？

方案我老早就开源了，就是用的换脸工作流里那一套模型，你只需要让 codex 帮你安装完，把自己的照片丢进去换脸就完事了。

** 当然要做足真人感，还要有些小技巧：**

喜欢折腾的自己去玩吧，当然还是建议真人出镜，在 ai 能复制一切的当下，你的活人感是你为数不多的不可替代性了。
